Based on the discussion in the ticket (and the StackExchange thread) the crux of this problem is that whenever your scaled image size comes out fractionally less than a whole pixel, `Math.round` will actually shrink one dimension of the image and crop off a row/column; instead we really want to guarantee that the image always “covers” the intended extent. In other words, for the *drawImage* call the width and height ought to be `Math.ceil`ed rather than `Math.round`ed. Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch that switches the two calls at the bottom of the drawImage invocation from `Math.round` to `Math.ceil`.  

```javascript
### src/ol/renderer/canvas/ImageLayer.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
      this.context.drawImage(
        img,
        0,
        0,
        +img.width,
        +img.height,
        Math.round(dx),
        Math.round(dy),
        Math.round(dw),
        Math.round(dh)
      );
=======
      this.context.drawImage(
        img,
        0,
        0,
        +img.width,
        +img.height,
        Math.round(dx),
        Math.round(dy),
        Math.ceil(dw),
        Math.ceil(dh)
      );
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With that change the image will never be shrunk by rounding down ― fractional sizes will always be rounded up, so you won’t inadvertently lose a row or column of pixels.
